mechanism_narrative: The final week breaks a three-week deterioration: RETAIL_REC rose from -44.9 to -42.3 while TRANSIT rose from -51.3 to -47.7 and WORKPLACES rose from -42.0 to -37.1 in the same week. A synchronised week-on-week improvement across three independent trip-purpose series marks a behavioural inflection rather than series-specific noise, so the four-week RETAIL_REC mean rises above the last four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 2.6 points, TRANSIT 3.6 points and WORKPLACES 4.9 points in the final week
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than -43.6 (its last-four-week mean) despite all three series improving in the final week.

mechanism_narrative: Commuting trips are the trip-chaining backbone for retail footfall. WORKPLACES is the only category that improved sharply in the final week (from -42.0 to -37.1). When the WORKPLACES weekly mean crosses above -39.0, office-bound workers resume en-route and lunchtime purchases, and RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks exceeds its trailing four-week mean.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean crosses above -39.0 (an improvement of at least 3 points from the -42.0 reading)
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -42.0 to -37.1 in the final week, the largest single-week gain of any category
failure_condition: In episodes where WORKPLACES crosses above -39.0, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days fails to exceed its trailing 28-day mean more than half the time.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS and TRANSIT rebounded together in the final week (PARKS from 11.6 to 22.4, TRANSIT from -51.3 to -47.7) after both fell in the prior week. Joint recovery of outdoor leisure and public-transport use means trips are being chained rather than being single-purpose outdoor outings, so discretionary retail stops are re-attached to those trips and RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean above 20.0 and TRANSIT weekly mean above -48.0 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and TRANSIT fell in week t-1w and both rebounded in week t-0w
failure_condition: When PARKS is above 20.0 and TRANSIT above -48.0, RETAIL_REC in the following two weeks does not rise relative to its trailing two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: Lengthening spring days and warmer weather pull discretionary leisure time outdoors, which PARKS captures at a positive 22.4 while RETAIL_REC remains at -42.3. With indoor retail capacity still constrained, outdoor time substitutes for in-store browsing, so the four-week RETAIL_REC mean stays at or below its trailing level even as total mobility improves.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at +22.4 remains the only category with a positive level while RETAIL_REC is -42.3
regime_hint: spring-to-summer outdoor season with indoor capacity limits
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its trailing 28-day mean while PARKS stays above 20.0, showing outdoor time did not substitute for in-store activity.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL fell from 13.9 to 11.9 in the final week while RETAIL_REC rose from -44.9 to -42.3, the signature of a relaxation of stay-at-home guidance: people leave home and immediately divert some of those trips to retail. Once the RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below 12.0 in the same week RETAIL_REC rises, the easing impulse continues to lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below 12.0 while RETAIL_REC rises week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL dropped 2.0 points and RETAIL_REC gained 2.6 points in the final week
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 12.0 with a same-week RETAIL_REC rise, yet RETAIL_REC over the following 28 days does not exceed its trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM sits at only -4.4 versus RETAIL_REC at -42.3, a 38-point gap that widened in the final week as grocery trips normalised and stockpiling behaviour faded. Closing of that gap marks the retreat of pandemic precaution, which frees household spend for discretionary categories; the pass-through to RETAIL_REC is fast and appears within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -7.3 to -4.4 in the final week, narrowing the gap to RETAIL_REC
failure_condition: In the week after GROCERY_PHARM narrows its gap to RETAIL_REC, RETAIL_REC does not rise week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The final-week RETAIL_REC bounce is not corroborated by transit: TRANSIT improved only to -47.7, still 3.9 points below its t-2w level of -48.6's prior-week slide and far below required trip volumes. Without a sustained transit recovery, retail trips lack the transport capacity to be realised, so the four-week RETAIL_REC mean ends below its trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean remains below -45.0 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has not exceeded -47.7 in any of the four observed weeks and is the deepest negative category
regime_hint: restrictions still binding on public transport
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its trailing 28-day mean while TRANSIT stays below -45.0 throughout, showing transit capacity was not binding.

mechanism_narrative: In the absence of a further policy step, home-based behaviour keeps retail demand suppressed: RESIDENTIAL at 11.9 is still 11.9 points above its pre-period baseline and RESIDENTIAL plus WORKPLACES together sum to roughly -25, showing a large share of the working day still spent at home. When the combined RESIDENTIAL-minus-WORKPLACES gap stays above 45 points, RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks does not recover.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL minus WORKPLACES weekly mean stays above 45.0 points
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL minus WORKPLACES equals 49.0 points in the final week (11.9 minus -37.1)
regime_hint: policy standstill with no further reopening step
